delete.description:
Revoke a token. Deletion is immediate and irreversible — the next request
carrying that token fails to resolve a user and gets a 401. The plugin scopes
the delete to the session user, so `id` can only ever name the caller's own
token; an id belonging to someone else reads back as "not found".

parameters.description: Id of one of the caller’s own tokens.

200.description: The token is revoked; requests carrying it now fail with 401.

403.description: The caller authenticated with an API token — revocation requires a session.

404.description: No such token belongs to the caller.

requestBody.description: Step 1 of a chat turn: SQL plus a formatted answer. Charts are a separate `POST /api/chat/visualize` call. Reuse one `conversation_id` for follow-up turns; an unknown UUID creates a conversation, while an ID owned by another user returns 404.

409.description: Relayed from the backend: a run is already in flight for this conversation, or the semantic layer has not been compiled yet.

post.description:
Same permission as the chat completions route: every chat user may trigger
this, not just admins.

Unlike the completions route, this one never creates a conversation: by the
time step 2 runs, step 1 (or `POST /api/conversations`) has already created
it. Falling back to create-on-missing here would leave an orphan
conversation — just the chart/table bubble, with no question or Message 1
ahead of it — whenever this is called with an id that never got that far
(e.g. a standalone API caller skipping the completions step).

requestBody.description: Step 2 of chat: the SQL and its already-executed result from step 1. A missing or unparseable body is tolerated — it degrades to `{ "charts": null }` rather than erroring, because the chart is a nice-to-have.

result.description: The executed SQL result — the `sql_response_from_db` from the step 1 answer. Either a one-item list holding a JSON-records string, or a list of row objects.

conversation_id.description: When given and owned by the caller, the result and any chart are appended to that conversation as an assistant message. Ignored by the backend; consumed by this handler only.

post.description:
Create a new CustomAnalysis with its Sql node.

Strict insert: input shape is enforced by :class:`CustomAnalysisCreate`
and the frontend is responsible for trimming and rejecting blank
values before sending. Updating an existing analysis goes through
``PUT /custom-analyses/{analysis_id}``.

Returns 409 when ``name`` or ``sql`` is already used by another
CustomAnalysis (both are unique natural keys), and 422 when the SQL
can't be parsed against the current catalog (no recognised tables) —
without those references the analysis would be invisible to
retrieval.

get.description:
Admin-only helper that fetches an OIDC provider's discovery document
server-side and returns the endpoints the SSO form needs.

Resolving the endpoints here (instead of letting Better Auth's SSO plugin
auto-discover from the issuer) lets us register providers with
`skipDiscovery: true`. For public IdPs that path requires no `trustedOrigins`
entry, so admins can add any provider without per-provider config.

Gated on sso:manage (admin) — it's an outbound fetch proxy.

parameters.name: issuer
parameters.description: HTTPS issuer URL; `/.well-known/openid-configuration` is appended.

200.description: The endpoints the SSO registration form needs, under their OpenID Connect Discovery names. `discovery_endpoint` is added by this route.

400.description: `issuer` is missing, unparseable, or not https.

401.description: No authenticated caller could be resolved

403.description: The caller lacks the required permission

502.description: The discovery endpoint answered non-2xx, or its document lacks `issuer`/`authorization_endpoint`/`token_endpoint`.

504.description: The discovery request timed out (8s) or could not be reached.

DescriptionSuggestionResponse.description: ``data`` is null when no description could be suggested.
DescriptionSuggestionResponse.title: DescriptionSuggestionResponse

EntityCoverageCandidate.description: One retrieved semantic candidate, ranked by vector distance.
EntityCoverageCandidate.title: EntityCoverageCandidate

max_distance.description: Maximum L2 vector distance for a candidate to count (lower score = closer match).
max_distance.title: Max Distance

EntityCoverageResult.description:
A 0–1 coverage grade with the candidates it was graded from.

``uncovered_entities`` is only present when the flow was asked for it.
EntityCoverageResult.title: EntityCoverageResult

ExplorationEdge.description:
Two tables connected by a shared SQL query and/or a foreign key.

``queries`` is empty for an edge that exists only because of a foreign
key; ``foreign_keys`` is empty for a SQL-only edge.
ExplorationEdge.title: ExplorationEdge

ExplorationRelatedNode.description: One related node. The catalog path fields are data-layer only.
ExplorationRelatedNode.title: ExplorationRelatedNode

ExplorationRelatedNodes.description: One page of related nodes; ``total`` counts every related node.
ExplorationRelatedNodes.title: ExplorationRelatedNodes

ExportRequest.description: Export scope: empty ``databases`` exports every catalog database.
ExportRequest.title: ExportRequest

ForeignKeyRef.description:
One foreign-key column pair behind an exploration edge.

``source_column`` always names a column on the edge's ``source``. The
sample values come straight off the Column node, unparsed — profiling
stores them as a JSON string, a catalog PATCH stores a list.
ForeignKeyRef.title: ForeignKeyRef

GraphLink.description: An undirected term↔term link (two terms sharing at least one table).
GraphLink.title: GraphLink

IdRef.description: ``{"id": ...}`` — echoed by the delete endpoints to confirm the target.
IdRef.title: IdRef

ModelFormat.description: Serialisation dialect of an exchanged model document.
ModelFormat.title: ModelFormat

NodeUpdateResult.description:
Echo of a catalog node patch: ``{id, ...the properties you sent}``.

``update_node_properties`` builds the body as ``{"id": ..., **{k: props[k]
for k in patch}}``, so only the keys the request actually patched come
back — every one of them is optional here for that reason, and each may be
null when the node has no value for it. The route as a whole answers null
when the patch was empty or the node does not exist.
NodeUpdateResult.title: NodeUpdateResult

PqlAnalysis.description: A verified PQL few-shot. The PQL text is a property, not a child node.
PqlAnalysis.title: PqlAnalysis

PublicConnection.description:
A UI-managed connection with its credentials stripped.

``connection`` is absent from the delete response, which echoes only the
database name it tore down; the list and create reads carry the full
credential-free config.
PublicConnection.title: PublicConnection

SchemasPayload.description: ``/schemas/{db_id}`` — unenveloped; null when the database is missing.
SchemasPayload.title: SchemasPayload

SchemaSummary.description: One schema of a database, with how many tables it holds.
SchemaSummary.title: SchemaSummary

SemanticExplorationGraph.description: ``{nodes, links}`` for the semantic layer, in one response.
SemanticExplorationGraph.title: SemanticExplorationGraph

SemanticGraphNode.description: A term on the semantic-layer exploration graph.
SemanticGraphNode.title: SemanticGraphNode

SqlAttribute.description:
A SqlAttribute with its owning Term and the SQL text behind it.

``zones`` is resolved only by the single-attribute read; ``sql_id`` and
``database_name`` only by the create/update writes.
SqlAttribute.title: SqlAttribute

SqlAttributePatchResponse.description: ``term_certification`` is recomputed only when the patch names a term.
SqlAttributePatchResponse.title: SqlAttributePatchResponse

SqlExpressionValidationResult.description: ``/sql-attributes/validate`` — a parse failure is a 422, not ``valid: false``.
SqlExpressionValidationResult.title: SqlExpressionValidationResult

SqlValidationResult.description: ``/custom-analyses/validate`` — a parse failure is a 422, not ``valid: false``.
SqlValidationResult.title: SqlValidationResult

SsoFederationState.description:
The one flag ``PATCH /connections/{database_name}/sso-federation`` sets.

The route deliberately echoes just the flag rather than the connection, so
a caller never has to re-send credentials to toggle it.
SsoFederationState.title: SsoFederationState

TableColumns.description:
A table with one page of its columns.

Every field but ``columns`` is absent from the empty fallback the route
returns when the table (or its schema/database path) is missing.
TableColumns.title: TableColumns

TableExplorationDetails.description: The table-detail modal: its SQL queries and one page of its Terms.
TableExplorationDetails.title: TableExplorationDetails

TableSqlQuery.description:
A stored SQL query that references the table.

``sql`` is nullable: unlike the other Sql reads in ``gsf/dal/exploration``
this query has no ``_NON_EMPTY_SQL`` filter, so a Sql node with a null or
blank ``sql_full_query`` reaches the response. Declaring it required would
turn that row into a 500 for the whole table-detail modal.
TableSqlQuery.title: TableSqlQuery

TableSummary.description: One table of a schema, with its column / SQL / Term counts.
TableSummary.title: TableSummary

Term.description: A Term with its certification rollup and resolved zone chips.
Term.title: Term

TermCountEntry.description: ``{term_id, count}`` — one per-term breakdown row. Zeroes are omitted.
TermCountEntry.title: TermCountEntry

TermDetail.description: One Term with the tables that represent it and its related terms.
TermDetail.title: TermDetail

TermListItem.description: A Term as it appears in the paged ``/terms`` list.
TermListItem.title: TermListItem

TermsPageResponse.description:
One page of the Terms list with its per-term count breakdowns.

``total`` counts every matching term; the count lists cover only the
terms on this page when a limit was given.
TermsPageResponse.title: TermsPageResponse

TermSummary.description: The three fields every Term projection carries.
TermSummary.title: TermSummary

TermTable.description: A table that REPRESENTS a Term, with its catalog path ids.
TermTable.title: TermTable

Zone.description:
A zone with its catalog data items.

``items`` is absent on the list endpoint, a list of ``ZoneItem`` on the
detail/update endpoints, and a plain list of the ids that were linked on
create.
Zone.title: Zone

ZoneChip.description:
A zone as rendered next to something else it grants access to.

``enabled`` is false for a zone whose ``Zone`` label was swapped for
``disableZone``; those are returned to admins only.
ZoneChip.title: ZoneChip

ZoneItem.description: A catalog node a zone grants access to (a database, schema or table).
ZoneItem.title: ZoneItem

ApiToken.name: x-api-key
ApiToken.description: A GSF API token (`gsf_…`), created under Account → API Tokens. The token carries its owner’s permissions. `Authorization: Bearer <token>` is accepted too.

SessionCookie.name: better-auth.session_token
SessionCookie.description: A browser session from an interactive sign-in. Only the few operations that manage API tokens require this — a token may not mint or revoke tokens.
